THoR maps each on-ice event to a 20-second goal-probability impact, then sums these impacts over a player's total ice time. This yields a net change in goal probability, converted to 'wins above average' via a linear transformation calibrated against historical goal rates. The method inherently corrects for zone starts by conditioning on observed shift locations, avoiding the confounding issues of traditional zone-start percentages. Failures arise when small-sample noise dominates signal, leading to unreliable win estimates; also when team lineup compositions systematically alter the context of events, violating the assumed additivity.
